newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada April manufacturers' shipments rise 0.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada April manufacturers' shipments rise 0.7 pct.

text.p: Canadian manufacturers' shipments rose 0.7 percent in April, to C$35.47 billion seasonally adjusted from a revised C$35.20 billion (C$35.35 billion) in March, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday.

Statistics Canada said manufacturers' shipments rose in April despite a decline in the motor vehicle sector, which dropped 2.0 percent. The drop was due mainly to slower activity because of U.S. labor disputes which left some Canadian plants short of key components.
The agency said the April rise in shipments resulted from a moderate but broad-based advance in most industries. Increases were recorded in 17 of 22 major industry groups.
StatsCan said the most significant increases were recorded for food (+2.0 percent), primary metal (+3.3 percent) and electrical and electronic products (+2.7 percent).
The agency said shipments of refined petroleum and coal products fell 3.8 percent, the third straight month for a drop.

But unfilled orders shot up 4.4 percent in the month to C$37 billion, breaking the previous high set two years ago, StatsCan said. April's rise is the largest in three years, a significant departure from a flat performance in 1996.
Transportation equipment recorded the biggest increase in orders, rising 9.2 percent.

Manufacturers' inventories rose for the third time in a row after two small declines in December and January, StatsCan said. The agency said inventories have remained in line with shipments since last spring's correction checked the steep growth from 1993 to 1995.
The increases in both shipments and inventories left the ratio unchanged for the fourth straight month, at a level close to the all-time lows of two years ago, StatsCan said.
The largest increases in inventories were in motor vehicle and parts (+6.8 percent) and machinery (+1.9 percent). The biggest drop was in refined petroleum and coal, down 4.9 percent.
